comments.body: RCA progress 2026-09-09: Phase 1 observation reconstructed from durable CI/Gerrit evidence. Failed run 34235734839 was change 2834 patchset 1. The failing job was require resolvable rebar ticket, and its checkout log shows the external checkout-gerrit-change-action first checked out the workflow dispatch ref from GitHub (`ref: 665d1d0480187380f82e59bd95af1f0c44274732`, the main/workflow ref), then tried `git fetch origin refs/changes/34/2834/1` (GitHub mirror does not advertise Gerrit refs), then fell back to `git fetch https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/rebar refs/changes/34/2834/1`, which failed immediately with HTTP 502. Gerrit later recovered; recheck run 34236969595 passed Verified, and change 2834 ultimately merged as 02e0fae923d45329a3e1dc1921d70e19484401b8. Working comparison: the patchset commit SHA itself (`d09bfdc154fe825ab0f8865c78f4f2c4f70c4590`) is fetchable from the GitHub mirror by object id, while `refs/changes/...` is not. Hypothesis H1: the failure class is not an invalid commit or bad trailer; it is the CI checkout helper treating Gerrit ref fetch as mandatory even when the patchset object is already mirrored by SHA, so a transient Gerrit HTTP 502/504 can fail Verified before any repository validation. Next experiment/fix should make Verified checkout prefer `GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION` from the GitHub mirror and only use Gerrit refspec as fallback, while verifying any fallback FETCH_HEAD equals the dispatch SHA.

comments.body: decision-needed after RCA 2026-09-09: I reconstructed the concrete CI failure and found a design fork before a safe implementation. Evidence: run 34235734839 failed in the checkout step before repository validation; log lines show the helper first checked out the workflow dispatch/main ref from GitHub (`ref: 665d1d0480187380f82e59bd95af1f0c44274732`), then `git fetch origin refs/changes/34/2834/1` failed because GitHub does not expose Gerrit change refs, then Gerrit fallback `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/rebar refs/changes/34/2834/1` returned HTTP 502. Gerrit recovered; recheck run 34236969595 passed and change 2834 merged as 02e0fae923d45329a3e1dc1921d70e19484401b8. I also fetched the third-party action source at the pinned SHA and confirmed this is its real algorithm: actions/checkout of `inputs.ref` (default `${{ github.sha }}`, i.e. the workflow ref), then mandatory Gerrit-refspec fetch from origin/Gerrit. Hypothesis confirmed for the checkout failure class: Verified depends on Gerrit being healthy because our mirror does not provide `refs/changes/*`, so transient Gerrit 502/504 can fail CI before tests. I did NOT claim or change code because the remediation choice is operator/design-sensitive. Options: (A) configure Gerrit→GitHub replication to publish `refs/changes/*`, preserving the current action and its intended mirror-first behavior; tradeoff: infra/Gerrit config change, but keeps CI YAML simple. (B) replace the action with an inline SHA-first checkout that fetches `GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION` from GitHub by object id then falls back to Gerrit and verifies FETCH_HEAD equals the dispatch SHA; tradeoff: portable in YAML if GitHub reliably serves pre-merge Gerrit objects by SHA, but that reachability must be proven/enforced. (C) accept Gerrit checkout 502/504 as infra-only and document `recheck` as the remedy; tradeoff: no code churn, but Verified remains sensitive to transient Gerrit outages. Recommended default: A if refs/changes replication to GitHub is acceptable; otherwise B only after an operator confirms pre-merge patchset SHA fetch is supported on the mirror. Specific question: should Verified be made independent of transient Gerrit HTTP availability by changing replication/checkout semantics, or should this remain an infra-retry class?

compiled_state.description:
## Context
During the comment-remediation epic, Gerrit briefly advertised `main` with parent `0fe2cc2e…` while Gitiles returned 404 for that object. Ref history appeared rewound and omitted merged commit `2a93f180…`. `git fetch gerrit main` returned timeout/HTTP 504, and CI run `34235734839` failed checkout when Gerrit returned HTTP 502 fetching change 2834. The service later recovered: the parent became readable and ref advertisement worked again.

This ticket owns the `/rebar-debug` investigation requested by the operator. RCA confirmed the actionable failure class: the pinned `checkout-gerrit-change-action` is mirror-first only when the GitHub mirror exposes the requested Gerrit change ref. Run 34235734839 showed GitHub lacked `refs/changes/34/2834/1`, forcing Gerrit fallback; the fallback returned HTTP 502 before repository validation. A later check found the ref visible on GitHub, proving the versioned refspec can work but that the live mirror can lag/miss until replication is triggered. The operator approved Option A: publish `refs/changes/*` to the org-private GitHub mirror and preserve the pinned action's mirror-first path.

## Operator ruling
Proceed with Option A and use push spec `+refs/changes/*:refs/changes/*`. This is an explicit accepted trade-off for the change-ref namespace only: branch/tag history remains non-force; `refs/meta/config` remains unreplicated via `replicatePermissions = false` and by avoiding wildcard `refs/*`. The force applies to patchset refs and `refs/changes/NN/NNNN/meta`; it is not what creates a missing ref, but it ensures the full replication sweep converges the mirrored change namespace even if Gerrit rewrites change metadata while preserving the one-way-door guard for `main`, tags, and feature branches.

## Plan
- Record the RCA/timeline on the ticket: run 34235734839 failed before validation because GitHub lacked `refs/changes/34/2834/1`; Gerrit fallback returned 502; recheck run 34236969595 later passed; current mirror checks show the change-ref namespace can be published.
- Update only the Gerrit change-ref replication spec to the operator-approved forced refspec `+refs/changes/*:refs/changes/*`, keeping `refs/heads/main`, `refs/tags/*`, `refs/heads/feature/*`, `projects = rebar`, `mirror = false`, and `replicatePermissions = false` intact.
- Amend the documentation/ADR consumers that currently describe the change-ref refspec as non-force: add a dated ADR-0021 amendment note and update `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md` so the docs state the bounded force trade-off for `refs/changes/*` while preserving the ADR-0010 one-way-door contract for branch/tag history and refs/meta/config privacy.
- Add a narrow repository test that parses `infra/gerrit/replication.config` and proves the exact forced change-ref refspec is present while the branch/tag/feature refspecs and privacy/safety filters remain unchanged.
- Apply the repository config on the Gerrit host through the supported replication setup/materialization path, snapshotting the live `replication.config` first. Use `docker compose exec gerrit gerrit plugin reload replication` if the plugin accepts reload; if not, use the minimal documented Gerrit restart only to load the config.
- Trigger full replication for remote `github` with the repo-documented Gerrit command `replication start --all --remote github --now --wait`, run from the host/container admin context (for example `docker compose exec gerrit ssh -p 29418 <admin>@localhost replication start --all --remote github --now --wait`, or the equivalent configured admin SSH). This is distinct from plugin reload: reload loads config; the replication start command backfills missing refs because `replicateOnStartup=false` deliberately does not do so.
- Monitor replication output/disk/CPU enough to catch obvious initial-load failures.
- Verify `refs/changes/*` visibility on GitHub with `git ls-remote`, spot-check an open change ref, and prove a CI-style `git fetch origin <refs/changes/...>` succeeds from the GitHub mirror without contacting Gerrit.
- Watch the first Mirror Guard run after the change and confirm it stays green with no replication-lag alarm.

## Testing
- RED: `pytest tests/scripts/test_gerrit_replication_config.py::<new refs_changes_refspec test>` fails before the config change because the file uses non-forced `refs/changes/*:refs/changes/*`.
- GREEN targeted: `pytest tests/scripts/test_gerrit_replication_config.py` plus `make config-check`.
- Final repository verification: `make verify PYTEST_WORKERS=2` with ambient GIT_CONFIG_* variables unset.
- Operational verification: after host apply and replication, `git ls-remote https://github.com/navapbc/rebar 'refs/changes/*'` returns change refs and a local fresh repo can `git fetch origin <open-change-ref>` from GitHub only.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The incident timeline is recorded on this ticket with exact Gerrit and CI evidence.
- [ ] The root cause is recorded on this ticket: the mirror-first action fell back to Gerrit because the GitHub mirror lacked the requested change ref at validation time.
- [ ] The versioned Gerrit replication config publishes `+refs/changes/*:refs/changes/*` while retaining main/tag/feature replication and refs/meta/config privacy controls.
- [ ] ADR/docs that previously documented non-force change-ref replication are updated to record the operator-approved scoped-force amendment and its safety boundaries.
- [ ] The live Gerrit host has the updated replication config applied and full replication has been triggered successfully.
- [ ] `refs/changes/*` visibility and a CI-style origin fetch are verified from the GitHub mirror without contacting Gerrit.
- [ ] Mirror Guard remains green after the change and no replication-lag alarm is observed.
